resources.string: Menu or race?\nWith separate layouts enabled, one ☰ button switches between them: the menu layout gives a four-way D-pad with ✓ and ←, the race layout gives left / right buttons and pedals. It never switches by itself. With one shared layout every button stays visible: a four-way D-pad steers and moves through menus, and ✓ / ← work in menus.

How does the mouse work?\nSlide on empty screen space to move the cursor. Lift after a slide without clicking. A short stationary tap clicks at the cursor position. Hold still to press and keep the button, then drag; lift to release. Multi-finger gestures do not click.

What does size change?\nGlobal size scales the default controls. In Edit positions & touch zones, drag a control and adjust Button to change its appearance, or Touch zone to change only where it responds. Dashed outlines show the touch zones; percentages are relative to the default control. Changes save automatically. The editor shows a grid; with Snap to grid on, a dragged control lands on it.

One layout or two?\nWith Separate menu and race layouts off, the same controls, positions and sizes are used in menus and races. Turn it on to customise each mode independently. Switching this option keeps both sets of saved layouts. Reset layout restores the selected set only. Steering on left / right mirrors both default and manually saved positions.

Edges and vertical position\nDistance from edges moves default controls inward. Raise driving controls moves the default lower controls upward. System cutouts are respected. Manually placed controls keep their saved positions.

Opacity and auto-hide\nOpacity sets normal visibility. Auto-hide starts after all fingers lift, after a delay of 1–30 seconds. Choose a faint silhouette or complete invisibility. Hidden buttons still respond on the first touch and become visible again. Holding a control prevents hiding. A press on a gamepad hides the controls at once; the next touch brings them back.

Manual gears\nShow gear − / + adds two optional buttons to the race layout. Enable manual transmission in the game. The keys they send are set in Controls → Touch → Keys and must match the game settings.

Vibration\nThe game\'s Force Feedback effects reach the phone and Gamepad 1. The game drives only one force-feedback device, so Gamepad 2 never vibrates. Phone vibration is switched on or off in Controls → Touch. Gamepad vibration is off until you switch it on in Controls → Gamepads; its strength is set in the game itself: Options → Controllers → Force Feedback. Effects come from the game, never from button taps.

Gamepads\nThe game always sees two gamepads: Gamepad 1 is player 1 together with the touch controls, Gamepad 2 is player 2. In Controls → Gamepads pick which pad is which by pressing a button on it and set what each button does, then press Gamepad ON once: it writes matching controls into the game\'s settings and backs up the old file. The left stick steers, the triggers accelerate and brake. To play on a keyboard, press Default in game instead.
Lights and recovery\n☼ sends L. ↻ sends R to return to the track. The keys can be changed in Controls → Touch → Keys.

Screen and game data\nLandscape locks the game horizontally; Auto permits rotation. FPS cap limits frame rate; a lower value can reduce work per second. Game data manages imports and shows which data set is active. Play is enabled when a data set is ready.
